blocker.summary: r468 did a static-analysis-only cycle (no processes launched, reread an already-captured log) to find what governs [ac6-visual-phase] world=1 in the oracle-hybrid ac6recomp binary. Ruled out the cheapest hypothesis first: the r452-style assets-only content-mount gap does NOT apply here -- run_gate.py passes the ISO directly as a positional arg, not via assets/. Found the exact detection mechanism: world=1 is stamped by NotifyWorldCompositorDraw() (render_hooks.cpp), called from exactly one site in command_processor.cpp:4204-4206, gated on a SINGLE pixel shader ucode hash (0x17e5e4ac3e713245) -- the same hash already known from r254's 'neutralize' deswizzle fix-payload list, not a coincidence. Rereading r465's already-captured 573s oracle log: 39 distinct pixel shaders were bound during the whole run, none matching this hash -- consistent with (not contradicting) the pre-existing campaign/world-transition ceiling r463-r467 already established, and weakens the alternative theory that the detector itself is just too narrow. This ceiling PREDATES the entire r454-r468 campaign (reports/retail-us-mission01-flight-long-candidate-20260828.md already documented the same ceiling back in August). Root cause of the campaign/world transition stall itself still not established. Named for r469: (1) find precisely where/why the campaign->world transition never fires (static Ghidra work on the transition code itself, or a gdb session targeted at that code instead of the now-ruled-out movie-worker thread); (2) recognize this ceiling may be substantial and out of scope for a single cycle -- if so, the PinnedShaderRuntime backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438/r454-r467, a different, unrelated native backlog) remains an independent non-blocking track. Native profile untouched this cycle (no rebuild occurred).
